auditor_value: w_parallel = 10 sin30 = 5 N (directed down the slope); w_perpendicular = 10 cos30 = 5 sqrt(3) = 8.66 N (into the slope)

findings.quote: component parallel to the slope = 5 N (up the slope)
findings.note: The along-slope component of a weight always points down the slope (the weight is vertical, so its component along the surface is toward the lower end). The magnitude 5 N is right; the direction annotation is false physics.
findings.fix: component parallel to the slope = 5 N (down the slope); component perpendicular to the slope = 8.66 N (into the slope)

findings.quote: The two components are at right angles to each other, so sine gives the along-slope part and cosine gives the into-slope part.
findings.note: That the components are perpendicular does not decide which one takes the sine. Sine goes with the along-slope part because the 30 deg angle is measured between the weight and the perpendicular component (step 1), so the perpendicular part is the adjacent side (cosine) and the along-slope part is the opposite side (sine).
findings.fix: The 30 deg angle lies between the weight and its perpendicular component, so the perpendicular component is the adjacent side, w cos30, and the along-slope component is the opposite side, w sin30.

question_defect: The figure description says w_parallel is 'directed up along the slope surface', which is impossible for a component of the weight; it is likely a misreading of the drawn vector triangle. The question text itself asks only for the two components.
notes: Both magnitudes (5 N and 8.66 N) agree with mine. The solution copied the figure description's 'up the slope' without comment; the brief treats following a defective figure description silently as a finding on the field that does so.
